originalTitle: The moment I knew: I heard her beautiful laugh again, and all my emotions came flooding back
summary: Eddie Botha felt an easy connection with Jennifer. But when she went away for a trip, he thought that was the end of their growing romance
content: I met Jennifer at a Guy Sebastian concert in Kuala Lumpur in 2005. It was strange I was there because I’m kind of anti-pop music, but we were introduced there by a mutual friend. We didn’t talk that much but I immediately liked Jen and invited her to dinner the following week. That first date wasn’t in a fancy restaurant and we sat in the corner and talked for over an hour. I liked that she wasn’t at all bothered by the simplicity of the dining room. Being a foreigner in Malaysia, I immediately felt with Jen that there wasn’t as much of a culture gap as I’d felt with others. I could talk to her easily and was struck by her warmth and openness. And it was there that I first heard her laugh beaming out across the room, a pure, joyous sound. A few weeks later I organised a weekend getaway to Kuantan with my friend Ivan, who had introduced us, and invited Jen along. I remember she was sort of jumping into the waves and fell backwards, and I caught her in my arms. I didn’t let go immediately and then I felt her hand on my shoulder, and then I heard that laugh again. It was a moment of unexpected intimacy that didn’t feel forced or contrived – almost as if nature pushed us towards each other. After that trip she went away with a girlfriend of hers to Bali and I thought maybe that was the end of things for us. Partly because her friend was a bit butch, I really wondered for a moment whether maybe they had gotten together on that trip – which of course I would have accepted. Then one day I was just getting home from work when, out of the blue, I saw her name appear on my phone. I was a bit surprised but very excited – we hadn’t spoken for two or three weeks. I hadn’t known I was going to hear from her again. She told me she’d had a wonderful trip away and had been thinking about me a lot. I expressed how happy I was to hear from her; that I had been thinking about her a lot as well and would love to see her again soon. In my nervousness I made some silly jokes. When I heard her beautiful, pure laugh again, and all my emotions came flooding back, I was certain she was the one for me. It was only a short call but it was enough to tell me everything I needed to know. After that we started spending more time together and would speak to each other on the phone for hours in the evenings. She stayed over at my place a few times. I knew Jen was always worried about how any guy would deal with meeting her eccentric father. When I met him, he was very flamboyant – brightly coloured clothes with lots of jewellery and bling. But I really liked him because I’m a bit eccentric myself. After three or four months, I asked Jen to marry me. She said no at first. She was only 21 at the time and I was 30. But a few months later, as we spent even more time together, she finally said yes, with her dad’s approval. We’ve been together for almost 20 years now, have two kids and live in Melbourne. Not to say we haven’t had any troubles. I’m the risk-taker and she’s very risk-averse. I think she is the voice of reason whereas I shoot from the hip. But I think she generally trusts my instincts. We have a healthy, balanced relationship. I love that she’s always believed in me as an artist. When we met in Malaysia I was working as a landscape architect. When we moved to Australia that fell to the wayside, so she encouraged me to venture more into the arts. She brings her business sense to my arts career. I admire her career as a CFO for a software company – I’ve had to let go of my old-fashioned instinct that the man should be the bread-winner. I am quite paternal and love spending more time with the kids. Our relationship is based on love and caring for each other – but I think our friendship is the real core that keeps us going. And she still has that beautiful, free flowing laugh, which brings our whole family so much joy. Eddie Botha’s work will feature as part of the Scotch Foundation Art Show, 10-13 September at James Forbes Academy, Scotch College Melbourne Tell us the moment you knew
chineseTitle: 我知道的那一刻：我再次听到她美丽的笑声，我所有的情绪都涌了回来
chineseSummary: 埃迪·博塔 (Eddie Botha) 觉得自己与詹妮弗 (Jennifer) 的关系很轻松。但当她去旅行时，他以为他们的浪漫就结束了
chineseContent: 2005 年，我在吉隆坡举办的盖伊·塞巴斯蒂安 (Guy Sebastian) 音乐会上认识了詹妮弗。我去那里感觉很奇怪，因为我是反流行音乐人，但我们是由一位共同的朋友介绍到那里的。我们没说太多，但我立刻喜欢上了珍，并邀请她下周共进晚餐。第一次约会不是在一家高档餐厅，我们坐在角落里聊了一个多小时。我喜欢她一点也不被餐厅的简单所困扰。作为马来西亚的外国人，我立即与 Jen 一起感受到，那里的文化差距并不像我与其他人一样大。我可以轻松地与她交谈，并被她的热情和开放所打动。正是在那里，我第一次听到她的笑声在房间里传出，一种纯净而快乐的声音。几周后，我和我的朋友 Ivan（他介绍了我们）一起组织了一次去关丹的周末度假，并邀请 Jen 一起去。我记得她当时正跳进海浪中，然后向后摔倒，我把她抱在怀里。我没有立即放开，然后我感觉到她的手放在我的肩膀上，然后我又听到了笑声。这是一个意想不到的亲密时刻，没有强迫或做作的感觉——几乎就像大自然将我们推向彼此。那次旅行之后，她和她的一个女朋友去了巴厘岛，我想也许我们的事情就结束了。部分原因是她的朋友有点粗鲁，我有一瞬间真的想知道他们是否在那次旅行中聚在一起——我当然会接受。有一天，我刚下班回家，突然间，我看到她的名字出现在我的手机上。我有点惊讶，但也很兴奋——我们已经两三个星期没有说话了。我不知道我会再次收到她的消息。她告诉我她度过了一次愉快的旅行并且一直在想
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
